channel.title: Ford recalls — Car Recall Tracker
channel.description: NHTSA vehicle safety recalls explained in plain English.

item.title: Ford Mustang Wiring Can Cause Power Loss
item.description: The engine compartment wiring harness has ground connections that can crack or break over time. If that happens, the vehicle can lose the power that keeps it moving forward. The same wiring problem can also cause other systems to stop working, including the windshield washers, the headlights, the air conditioning, or the engine cooling fan, depending on which connection is affected.

item.title: Ford F-650 Liftgate Deck Pins May Break
item.description: On this truck, the deck pins that hold the liftgate platform in place may break. If a pin breaks, the liftgate platform can fall unexpectedly, which increases the risk of injury to anyone nearby.

item.title: Ford Explorer, Lincoln Aviator Seats May Recline
item.description: Some Ford Explorer and Lincoln Aviator vehicles have a driver's seat that may recline on its own when no one is sitting in it, such as when the vehicle is remotely unlocked or remotely started. If the seat back moves unexpectedly, it could trap a person sitting in the second row.

item.title: Ford Bronco Engine Wiring Can Short Circuit
item.description: The wiring harness in the engine compartment of your Ford Bronco or Bronco Raptor may become damaged. If the wiring is damaged, it can short-circuit, meaning electricity arcs where it shouldn't. This can create heat or a spark in the engine compartment.

item.title: Ford Explorer Roof Rail Covers May Detach
item.description: On certain Ford Explorer vehicles, the covers on the roof rails may come loose and detach from the vehicle.

item.title: Ford, Lincoln Second-Row Seats May Shift Unexpectedly
item.description: Ford is recalling certain Explorer and Lincoln Aviator vehicles because the switch for the easy-entry second-row outer seats may bind or stick. This can cause the seat to unlatch, tip, or slide unexpectedly. A seat that moves unexpectedly may not properly restrain a passenger in a crash. This is a phased recall — the repair will become available at different times depending on the model and model year. Dealers will inspect and replace the switch bezel as necessary, at no cost.

item.title: Ford Mustang Wipers May Fail in Cold Weather
item.description: Some Mustang and Mustang GTD vehicles can have trouble with the windshield wipers and washer system in cold temperatures. The wipers may only work on their high-speed setting, and the washer fluid system may not spray properly. Both of these problems can make it harder to see clearly out of the windshield.

item.title: Ford, Lincoln SUVs: Transmission Park System May Fail
item.description: On affected vehicles, a part called the park pawl, which is supposed to lock the transmission in place when you put the vehicle in park, may engage while the vehicle is still moving. This can damage the park system, the mechanism that normally keeps the vehicle from rolling once it has been shifted into park.

item.title: Ford Bronco Fender Flares May Detach
item.description: Ford is recalling certain Bronco vehicles because the fender flares may not be properly secured. A fender flare that isn't secured well enough can detach from the vehicle. A detached fender flare can end up on the road as a hazard for other vehicles.

item.title: Ford Mustang, Lincoln Nautilus, Navigator Instrument Cluster Blank
item.description: Ford is recalling certain 2019 Mustang, Nautilus, and Navigator vehicles because an earlier repair for this same problem did not fully fix it. When the vehicle is started, the instrument panel display may fail to work and show a blank screen instead of turning on. This means the gauges and warning lights on the dashboard may not be visible to the driver.

item.title: Ford Focus/Fusion Clutch Failure May Cause Fire
item.description: Ford is recalling certain Focus and Fusion vehicles because two earlier repairs for this problem did not fully fix it. The clutch inside the transmission may crack or break, which can damage the transmission and cause a fluid leak. If that leaked fluid reaches a hot part of the engine or exhaust, it could ignite. Ford has sent owners an interim letter about this fire risk while it finishes developing the full repair for this problem.

item.title: Ford Focus Fuel System Valve May Stall Engine
item.description: Ford is recalling certain Focus vehicles because an earlier repair for this same defect did not fully correct it. A valve in the fuel system, called the canister purge valve, may malfunction and cause the engine to stall unexpectedly while you are driving. This is the same underlying issue that a previous recall was supposed to fix, but that repair did not resolve the problem completely, so affected vehicles still have the risk of an unexpected engine stall while on the road.

item.title: Ford F-150 Daytime Running Lights Fail to Dim
item.description: Ford is recalling certain F-150 trucks because an earlier repair for this exact problem did not fully fix it. When the headlight switch is turned from 'Autolamps' to 'Headlamps On,' the daytime running lights may stay fully bright instead of dimming down to parking lights as they're supposed to. In other words, the lights don't switch modes correctly when the driver changes this setting.

item.title: Ford F-150 Transmission May Select Wrong Gear
item.description: Ford is recalling certain F-150 trucks because an earlier repair for this issue did not fully correct it. If the shift lever is moved quickly from Park to Drive, the instrument cluster may briefly lose the gear indicator display, and the transmission may momentarily select an unintended gear, such as Reverse or Neutral, instead of the gear you chose. This can happen even though the driver intended a different gear.

item.title: Ford Expedition: Center Console May Have Sharp Edges
item.description: On certain Ford Expedition SUVs, the chrome plating on the center console may bubble and peel, which can leave sharp edges exposed. Vehicle occupants may come into contact with these sharp edges, increasing the risk of injury. Dealers will inspect the center consoles and replace them as necessary, and this repair will be done at no cost to the owner as part of the recall.

item.title: Ford Explorer Park System May Fail, Rollaway Risk
item.description: Ford is recalling certain Explorer vehicles equipped with a specific engine and transmission combination. The vehicle's powertrain computer may unexpectedly reset itself while the vehicle is being driven, and this can damage the parking system. If the parking system is damaged, the vehicle may not be able to shift into Park. A vehicle that can't be shifted into Park may roll away on its own if left unattended.

item.title: Ford Expedition, Lincoln Navigator Seat Belt May Lock
item.description: Certain Ford Expedition and Lincoln Navigator vehicles have a problem with the seat belt pretensioner in the driver's seat, the front passenger seat, or both. The pretensioner may inadvertently lock the seat belt, which then will not retract or extend the way it normally should.

item.title: Ford Explorer Engine May Fail Suddenly
item.description: The engine in these vehicles may fail while you are driving. If the engine fails, it can suddenly cut off power to the wheels, meaning the vehicle can no longer keep moving under its own power.

item.title: Bronco Sport, Maverick Front Suspension Detachment Risk
item.description: Some Ford Bronco Sport and Maverick vehicles may have front lower control arm ball joints that were installed or repaired incorrectly at the assembly plant. This can allow the control arm to disconnect from the front wheel. A detached control arm can cause a loss of vehicle control, increasing the risk of a crash.

item.title: Ford Bronco Hardtop Roof Panels May Detach
item.description: On certain Ford Bronco vehicles, the molded hardtop roof panels may not have been made correctly. Because of this manufacturing problem, parts of the outer roof panel can come loose and separate from the vehicle. A section of roof breaking away and landing on the road creates a hazard for the Bronco and for other drivers, increasing the risk of a crash.

item.title: Ford Bronco Front Seat Bolt May Come Loose
item.description: Ford is recalling certain 2024-2026 Ranger and Bronco vehicles. The front seats may have a height-adjustment pivot bolt that is loose or has come dislodged.

item.title: Ford Bronco Transmission-to-Transfer Case Joint May Wear
item.description: Some Ford Bronco vehicles may have a joint between the transmission and transfer case that is out of alignment because of a previous repair that wasn't done correctly. This misalignment can cause the connecting parts at that joint to wear down more than normal over time. If the wear becomes severe enough, it can affect how power gets delivered from the transmission to the wheels.

item.title: Ford F-53 and F-59 Missing Front Wheel Hub Nut
item.description: On certain Ford F-53 and F-59 vehicles, the front axle hub assembly on the wheels may be missing a nut and a small pin that are supposed to be installed there to hold everything together properly. If this hardware is missing, the brakes on that wheel could be damaged, or the wheel could become loose and separate from the vehicle while it is being driven.

item.title: Ford, Lincoln Windshield Wiper Arms May Break
item.description: Ford is recalling certain Expedition, F-250 SD, F-350 SD, F-450 SD, F-550 SD, F-600 SD, and Lincoln Navigator vehicles because the windshield wiper arms may break. When a wiper arm breaks, the windshield wipers can fail to work properly, which can make it harder for the driver to see the road ahead. Dealers will inspect the wiper arms on affected vehicles and replace them if necessary, at no cost to the owner.

item.title: Ford Explorer and Lincoln Models Camera and ADAS Loss
item.description: In these Ford Explorer and Lincoln vehicles, a part called the Image Processing Module A may unexpectedly reset itself multiple times. When this module resets, it can cause the vehicle to lose the rearview camera image. It can also cause the vehicle to lose several driver assistance features at the same time, including pre-collision assist, lane-keeping assist, and blind-spot monitoring.

item.title: Ford Super Duty Fuel Pump May Fail Again
item.description: Ford is recalling certain F-250 SD, F-350 SD, F-450 SD, F-550 SD, F-600 SD, and F-750 Super Duty trucks that were previously repaired incorrectly under recall 24V957. Biodiesel deposits may build up on the fuel pump's drivetrain roller components, which could cause the high-pressure fuel pump to fail. A fuel pump failure can cause a loss of drive power. Dealers will update the powertrain control module software, at no cost to the owner.

item.title: Ford F-53 and F-59 brake lights may stay lit
item.description: Ford is recalling certain 2025-2026 F-59 and F-53 commercial stripped chassis vehicles. The brake lights on the outside of the vehicle may stay lit even when the driver is not pressing the brakes. Because of this, the vehicles do not meet the federal safety rule for lamps, reflective devices and related equipment. Dealers will inspect the brake pedal and repair the brake booster push rod if needed, free of charge. Owner notification letters were mailed March 27, 2026.

item.title: Ford, Lincoln Seat Belt Anchor Bolts May Loosen
item.description: Ford is recalling certain Explorer and Lincoln Aviator vehicles because the seat belt anchor bolts at the second-row outer seating positions may not be properly secured. A loose seat belt buckle may not properly restrain a passenger during a crash. Dealers will inspect the second-row outer seat belt lower anchor bolts and repair or replace them as necessary, at no cost to the owner.

item.title: Ford F-350 driveshaft weld may fail suddenly
item.description: On certain Ford F-250 SD and F-350 SD trucks, a weld on the rear driveshaft may fail. If it does, the driveshaft can separate and the truck can suddenly lose the power that drives the wheels. This sudden loss of power while driving raises the risk of a crash. Dealers will inspect the driveshaft and replace it if needed, at no cost to the owner.

item.title: Ford E-450 backup alarm may stop working
item.description: On certain Ford E-350 and E-450 vans, the connector for the backup alarm can come loose and disconnect. When that happens, the alarm will not sound while the vehicle is backing up. Pedestrians and people in other vehicles may not be warned that the van is reversing, which raises the risk of a crash or injury. Dealers will replace the connector on the wiring harness at no cost to the owner.

item.title: Ford, Lincoln Wiper Motor May Fail To Work
item.description: Ford is recalling certain Explorer, Escape, Lincoln Aviator, and Lincoln Corsair vehicles because the windshield wiper motor may fail. If the motor fails, the windshield wipers may stop working properly, which can make it harder for the driver to see the road. Dealers will inspect the front wiper motors and replace them if necessary, at no cost to the owner. A final repair is expected to be available in October 2026.

item.title: Ford Explorer headlight turns wrong way in curves
item.description: Ford is recalling certain 2025 and 2026 Explorer vehicles. Software for the system that turns the headlights as the vehicle goes through curves can point the passenger-side headlight in the wrong direction. Because of this, the vehicles do not meet the federal safety standard covering lamps, reflective devices and related equipment. A dealer can update the headlight control module software, or the update can be sent to the vehicle over the air.

item.title: Ford Explorer, Mustang, Nautilus EGR Valve Failure
item.description: The exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) valve in your vehicle may fail. If that happens, you could unexpectedly lose drive power while you're driving down the road. Dealers will replace the EGR valve, free of charge. Owner notification letters have already been mailed to affected owners.

item.title: Ford Bronco, Edge Rearview Camera May Fail
item.description: Certain Bronco and Edge vehicles have a computer module that helps run features like the rearview camera. This module can overheat and shut down. When that happens, the rearview camera image may not display the way it should. This means the driver may not get a view behind the vehicle when needed.

item.title: Ford and Lincoln Rearview Camera Image May Invert
item.description: The image on the center display may flip or turn upside down, showing an incorrect rearview image when the vehicle is put into reverse. Because the rearview image is not displayed correctly, these vehicles do not meet federal safety standards for rear visibility. To fix the problem, Ford dealers will update the software in the accessory protocol interface module at no charge to the owner.

item.title: Ford Explorer Rear Suspension Toe Link May Fracture
item.description: Ford says a part of the rear suspension called a toe link may fracture, or break, on certain Explorer vehicles. If a toe link fractures, the driver can lose control of the vehicle's steering. This loss of steering control raises the chance of a crash while driving.

item.title: Ford and Lincoln Trailer Brake and Light Failure
item.description: When towing a trailer, the integrated trailer module in certain Ford and Lincoln vehicles may lose communication with the vehicle. This can cause a loss of trailer brake and turn signal lights, or a loss of trailer brake function.

item.title: Ford Escape and Lincoln Corsair Hybrid Battery Defect
item.description: On these Ford Escape and Lincoln Corsair plug-in hybrid vehicles, a manufacturing defect in one or more high voltage battery cells may cause an internal short circuit and battery failure.

item.title: Ford F-53 Brake Lights May Malfunction
item.description: The exterior brake lights on some Ford F-53 and F-59 vehicles may turn on when they shouldn't or fail to turn on when the brake pedal is pressed, because a switch was installed incorrectly. This same issue may also let the vehicle be shifted out of park without the brake pedal being applied.

item.title: Ford Escape and Focus Block Heater Fire Risk
item.description: The engine block heater in some Ford Escape and Focus vehicles can crack over time and leak coolant. If coolant leaks while the heater is plugged in, it can cause an electrical short circuit inside the heater. This short circuit raises the chance that a fire could start in the vehicle.
